topic: AI Search Visibility and Brand Discovery
headline: AI Knows Your Brand – It Rarely Puts You On The Shortlist via @sejournal, @gregjarboe
keyNotes: Even if AI knows who you are, it might not recommend your business; one person found his newsletter was never recommended in 12 categories, and his advisory firm only once out of 43 times, despite AI knowing his career.
More than half of business buyers (51%) now start their research with AI chatbots, and most of them (69%) end up choosing a different company than they originally planned because of the chatbot.

Businesses used to focus on just being 'discoverable' online, meaning getting found easily, but now it's more important for AI to actually suggest your company when someone asks for solutions, not just know about you.

AI often uses old information, like past job titles or old press releases, to decide what to recommend, meaning what the AI says about you might not be current, and only 29% of marketers are actively checking this.

AI tends to recommend companies that provide the clearest explanations of a topic, rather than the company that first came up with the idea, and it often gets its recommendations from existing 'best of' lists published by other websites.
question: Considering Tony Uphoff's finding that AI knows who he is but rarely recommends his current businesses, how might your own company ensure AI recommends your most relevant and current offerings, rather than just knowing your past?
